title: "ENOUGH IS ENOUGH": Winnipeggers demand justice for tragic shooting of Nigerian student
article: Winnipeggers took to the street on Saturday afternoon to demand justice for the tragic shooting of a 19-year-old Nigerian student by Winnipeg Police on New Year\'s Eve.
Beginning at Union Station, a solidarity walk headed down Broadway to the Manitoba Legislative Building for speeches before continuing on the Winnipeg Police headquarters.

Afolabi Stephen Opaso, an international economics undergraduate student at the University of Manitoba from Nigeria died after police officers were called to an apartment suite in the first 100 block of University Crescent for reports of a man acting erratically and encountered Opaso armed with two knives. However, a lawyer for Opaso\'s family said he was having a mental breakdown and there is no indication he attacked police.

"We are here to rally and make our demands to the powers that be and all levels of government to do police reform and stop the killing of black people and people of colour in general," said Titi Tijani, president of African Communities of Manitoba Inc. (ACOMI), the umbrella organization for all African organization in Manitoba, which organized the walk along with the Nigerian Association of Manitoba, the student association and Opaso\'s family.

Tijani recalled a similar event in February 2019 when a South Sudanese refugee named Machuar Mawien Madut was fatally shot by Winnipeg Police during a mental health crisis at his suite in an apartment building on Colony Street near Broadway, not far from the Legislative Building. She called on the Independent Investigation Unit of Manitoba to ensure that a transparent investigation into Opaso\'s death in conducted.

"This must stop. Enough is enough," said Tijani, noting that there was a call for an inquest into Madut\'s death which might have made recommendations to prevent it from happening again. "The IIU needs to be accountable and transparent in their investigation and treat everybody\'s lives - particularly lives of people of colour because we are a minority - the same way as any other Manitoban. Enough is enough. Police brutality, racial profiling, this needs to stop.
"We did the same thing (five years ago). Why should we continue to do this? It needs to stop."

The investigation into this case is being handled by Alberta\'s police watch dog after the IIU handed it off to them after learning one of the officers involved in the shooting is closely related to a Manitoba Justice employee.

"We need police to be accountable, the same way they are holding everyone else accountable," said Tijani. "They need to respect the law. They are not be above the law just because they have guns. Enough is enough. We need every level of government to stop the killing, stop the racial profiling. We are taxpayers and this is our country. Taking the lives of our people has to stop.
"We have children and we are afraid. I\'m a mother and I\'m afraid for my boys for when they go out and come into contact with the police."
Tijani remembers having \'the talk\' with her children on if they have an encounter with the police.
